# BLO-29526 — env-guard helper-path hint derived from the guard's own directory

[BLO-29526](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-29526) ·
[#2219](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/2219)

## Files

- `src/server/env-guard.ts`
- `src/server/env-guard.test.ts`

## What changed and why

The env-guard blocks full-environment dumps and suggests `safe-env-inspect.mjs`
as the sanctioned alternative. The installer (`buildEnvGuardSetupShell`) writes
both scripts into `GUARD_DIR`, which is `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when that is set,
but the block message built its suggested path from `process.env.HOME`. Agent
pods do set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to a session directory outside `$HOME`, so the
two never agreed in production and the emitted command was always a path that
does not exist.

The failure mode is what made it worth fixing rather than knowing: the
suggestion is routinely piped into a filter, so `node` fails on stderr, a
`2>/dev/null` discards it, and the pipeline exits silently with no output —
indistinguishable from "no variable matches", i.e. a confident wrong negative an
agent will act on.

The hint is now derived as a sibling of the guard's own module
(`new URL("safe-env-inspect.mjs", import.meta.url)`) and reads no environment at
all. `installOnce()` writes both files into one directory, so the two paths
cannot drift again. The derivation sits inside the stdin handler, under the
existing fail-open `catch`, so a guard error still cannot wedge a run. The path
is POSIX single-quoted, since a config directory may contain spaces.

The regression test runs the emitted command rather than asserting on the
message string, so it fails if the install target moves — asserting on the
string alone would not. It also pins a non-obvious fact: what permits the
suggestion past the guard is `containsDump()` returning false, **not**
`SAFE_ENV_INSPECTION_RE`, which does not match the quoted form at all. A future
tightening of that allowlist would otherwise show no red test.
